chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub said: Ibn Bukayr informed me from Zurarah, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying:
"And for each [inheritance category], We made heirs from what the parents and close relatives left."

He said: 'He meant by this the close relatives (of kinship) in inheritance, and did not mean the beneficiaries of favors; therefore, the most entitled to the deceased are those closest to him in the womb that connects him to it.'

key_terms.أَوْلِيَاءَ اَلنِّعْمَةِ: Beneficiaries of favors (those who received gifts or kindness, often contrasted with blood relatives in legal contexts)
key_terms.أُولِي اَلْأَرْحَامِ: Close relatives by kinship (specifically those with a blood tie but not in the primary fixed shares)

ai.seo_question: What does the Quranic term 'mawali' refer to in the context of inheritance according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the interpretation of the verse regarding 'heirs' (mawali), distinguishing 'ul al-arham (close kin by blood) from awliya al-ni'mah (those who received favors). He establishes that the primary criterion for inheritance entitlement is the closeness of the familial bond (rahim) connecting the heir to the deceased, a nuance critical to Shia jurisprudence on kinship-based inheritance shares.
